result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers a plain `mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`. I haven't tested any of those folder names against the new rule.

The change is in `addMockResourcesConventions()` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`. The two folder regexes went from `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` to `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`, and the same for `__mock`.

- **Single folder name:** `[^/]*` stops at the next slash, so the match stays inside one folder name. It still needs a `/` right before `mock`, so `remock/` and `demo/` are not matched. Files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` are not matched either, since the rule needs a trailing `/` after the folder name.
- **Previously matched folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already turns backslashes into slashes before matching, so Windows-style paths work without further change.

I ran `mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test -Dtest='ScopingConventions*'`, which printed nothing. The `-Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` flag makes Maven pass quietly when no test matches that name, so I can't tell whether any test ran. I didn't add tests.
